$comment: Feed this to Gemini / Nano Banana Pro to generate the RideIQ system-architecture diagram. Use 'image_prompt' as the main instruction and 'spec' as the exact structure. Architecture description only.

meta.subtitle: Self-hosted, ML-powered navigation + ride-hailing app (Android + FastAPI), deployed to AWS EC2 with blue-green CI/CD

image_prompt: Create a clean, professional high-level software architecture diagram, left-to-right flow, flat modern style, rounded rectangles, soft shadows, clearly labeled arrows. Four vertical zones separated by faint dashed boundaries. ZONE 1 CLIENT: an Android phone showing the RideIQ map app with a search bar, a Drive/Walk toggle, and route-option cards; list its three tabs (Map, Insights, Profile); show it also pulls free map tiles directly from OpenStreetMap. ZONE 2 CI/CD PIPELINE: GitHub push to main triggers GitHub Actions, which builds a Docker image, pushes it to the ghcr.io registry, and SSHes into the server to run a blue-green deploy; include a small rollback loop and a separate 'build-city-graph' job that produces the road-graph files. ZONE 3 AWS EC2 HOST: an nginx reverse proxy on port 80 in front of two app containers labeled rideiq-blue and rideiq-green (only one live at a time; draw green solid/active, blue faded/idle), a shared Redis cache, a SQLite database on a mounted volume, and two baked-in graph files (city_graph.json for driving, walk_graph.json for walking). ZONE 4 BACKEND BRAIN (inside the live container): a FastAPI service exposing REST endpoints, an A* routing engine, and a stack of machine-learning models. Show the request path as a bold arrow: phone -> Elastic public IP -> nginx :80 -> live container :8000 -> routing engine + ML models -> back to the phone. Show an external call from the backend to OpenStreetMap Nominatim for address search and geocoding. Add a legend: green = active version, grey = idle/rollback, one arrow style for user traffic and another for the CI/CD deploy path. Keep every arrow labeled with its protocol (HTTPS/HTTP, SSH, Docker pull, Redis, SQLite, REST).

style.shapes: rounded rectangles for services, cylinder for databases, phone frame for client, dashed box for the EC2 host boundary

legend.means: idle version kept for instant rollback

components.label: RideIQ Android app
components.tech: Java, osmdroid (OpenStreetMap), Retrofit, TextToSpeech, Fused/GPS location
components.placement: Runs on the user's phone; the only user-facing piece.
components.description: Three tabs via bottom navigation. MAP (home): search bar with live autocomplete, Drive/Walk segmented toggle, tap-or-type pickup/drop-off, up to three route-option cards (recommended + slower alternatives with ETA, fare, arrival time), and turn-by-turn voice navigation that follows live GPS. INSIGHTS: the ML analytics screens. PROFILE: settings. Draws its own map from free OSM tiles and speaks directions with a male, faster voice.

components.label: OSM map tiles (CARTO / Esri)
components.placement: Fetched directly by the app, not through the backend.
components.description: Free street and satellite map imagery rendered under the route and markers. No Google Maps, no API key.

components.label: GitHub Actions
components.placement: Runs in GitHub's cloud on every push to main.
components.description: deploy-rideiq: builds the backend Docker image and orchestrates the deploy. build-city-graph: a manual job that downloads OpenStreetMap roads (drive or walk) with osmnx and commits the graph files, which re-triggers a deploy.

components.label: ghcr.io container registry
components.placement: Cloud registry between build and deploy.
components.description: Stores each built image tagged by commit SHA plus 'latest'. The EC2 host pulls images from here. Rollback = redeploying an older SHA tag.

components.label: nginx edge (port 80)
components.placement: The single public door on the EC2 host.
components.description: Reverse proxy on port 80. Routes all traffic to whichever app container is currently live, and is switched during a blue-green deploy. Only port 80 is exposed publicly.

components.label: rideiq-blue
components.placement: One of two interchangeable app containers on the private docker network.
components.description: The previous version, kept idle and ready for instant rollback.

components.label: rideiq-green
components.placement: The currently live app container behind nginx.
components.description: Serves all requests. During deploy, the new color is health-checked before nginx switches to it, so a bad release never reaches users (zero downtime).

components.label: Redis
components.placement: Shared container on the private network; never swapped.
components.description: Caches repeated answers (analytics plots, identical quotes, geocoding results) so the app stays fast and external geocoder calls stay within rate limits.

components.label: SQLite (rideiq.db)
components.tech: SQLite on a mounted Docker volume
components.placement: Persisted on a host volume so it survives deploys.
components.description: Logs every quote (distance, ETA, fare, cancellation risk, timestamp). The planned scaling step replaces this with Postgres for many concurrent users.

components.label: Road graphs (city_graph.json, walk_graph.json)
components.tech: OpenStreetMap-derived JSON graphs, baked into the image
components.placement: Bundled inside the backend image at build time.
components.description: Two routable networks for Edmonton: a drivable-roads graph and a footpaths/sidewalks graph, each with intersections, street shapes, lengths, and names. Produced by the build-city-graph workflow.

components.label: FastAPI REST service
components.placement: The application inside the live container.
components.description: Exposes the endpoints the app calls: /route and /route-latlon (mode-aware routing with alternatives), /quote, /geocode and /search (address lookup), /reverse-geocode, /landmarks, the analytics endpoints, plus /health and /metrics. Auto-generates interactive docs at /docs.

components.label: A* routing engine
components.tech: A* search (Dijkstra + haversine heuristic), penalized re-runs for alternatives
components.placement: Called by the routing endpoints inside FastAPI.
components.description: Finds the shortest path over the drive or walk graph, traces real street shapes, generates turn-by-turn steps with street names, and produces up to three distinct routes by penalizing already-used roads and re-running.

components.label: ML brain (15 models, 8 features)
components.placement: Trained once at container startup; called per request.
components.description: ETA prediction (Linear Regression + Random Forest + Neural Network), fare estimation (Random Forest + KNN), cancellation risk (Logistic + Decision Tree + AdaBoost), fraud check (SVM + Naive Bayes), surge zones (K-Means + Gaussian Mixture + Hierarchical), rider segments (PCA + LDA), driver-shift analysis (Hidden Markov Model), and cancellation causes (Bayesian Network).

components.label: OSM Nominatim geocoder
components.placement: External service the backend calls (and caches).
components.description: Turns typed addresses into coordinates (/search, /geocode) and coordinates into addresses (/reverse-geocode), biased to Edmonton. Cached in Redis to respect its rate limit.

request_flow: 1. User types or taps a destination; the app calls /search for live autocomplete.
2. App requests a route (/route-latlon) with the chosen mode (drive or walk).
3. nginx forwards to the live container; FastAPI runs A* on the matching graph and prices it with the ML models, returning the best route plus alternatives.
4. The app shows route-option cards; the user picks one and taps Start trip.
5. The app follows live GPS, speaks each turn, and announces arrival at the destination.
annotations: Only one app color (blue/green) serves traffic at a time; the other is the rollback safety net.
The new version must pass a /health check before nginx switches to it -> zero-downtime deploys.
Maps and routing use only free OpenStreetMap data -- no Google Maps and no API key.
Redis (cache), the SQLite volume, and the baked-in graph files are the stateful/asset pieces that persist across deploys.
